name: SOMATOM CounT research photon-counting CT
description: Siemens adapted a research whole-body dual-source scanner to compare direct photon-counting CT with conventional energy-integrating CT. One detector chain retained an energy-integrating array and the other used a cadmium telluride photon-counting array.

date.basis: Mayo Clinic gives the installation year.

events.statement: Mayo Clinic installed the investigational SOMATOM CounT scanner in Rochester, Minnesota.

evidence.supports: Identifies the installed 2014 prototype by name.
The Mayo-led study identifies the laboratory system as the hybrid whole-body photon-counting scanner.

date.label: by 2015-11-24
date.basis: Submission of the completed human study supplies an upper bound on the scans.

events.statement: At the NIH Clinical Center, researchers obtained photon-counting and energy-integrating abdominal CT images in a study of 15 volunteers.
events.caveats: Research-volunteer enrollment ran from September through November 2015. The source does not date the first scan or establish clinical service.

evidence.locator: Abstract, Materials and Methods; Submission history
evidence.supports: Documents completed scans in the bounded study and the manuscript submission date.

earliest_record.rationale: Mayo identifies the prototype and installation year. Its later NIH imaging is documented by a separate clinical study.

links.statement: Siemens built the hybrid research scanner on the SOMATOM Definition Flash platform, replacing one of its conventional detector chains with a photon-counting chain.
links.scope: Physical platform and detector substitution in the investigational system.

evidence.supports: Explicitly names the Definition Flash basis and the EID–PCD pairing.
The separate NIH study confirms the mixed detector configuration of its prototype.
